key_insight: Cell-type-focused polygenic risk scores reveal that neurodegenerative disease genetics are partly shared across brain cell types, but also retain disease-specific patterns, especially for Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease with dementia, Parkinson’s without dementia, and ALS.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help researchers better stratify neurodegenerative risk and distinguish overlapping dementia-related biology, but they are not yet ready for direct clinical use.
method: Analyzed polygenic risk scores in UK Biobank across multiple neurodegenerative diseases.
Restricted genetic analyses to genes reported in major brain cell types: microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and neurons.
Compared cell-type-specific scores and APOE-related effects across disease phenotypes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports substantial overlap among cell-type gene sets (21-29%) and that combined cell-type PRSs explained 60-93% of genetic liability for NDDs with major dementia involvement.
watch_item: Current cell-type gene annotations overlap heavily, so these PRS signals may reflect shared genetics rather than cleanly separated cell-specific biology.
paper_title: Mapping polygenic risk scores to brain cells: insights for neurodegenerative diseases
